repository.description: The open-source Claude Motion & CapCut alternative. Turn a reference video into editable motion graphics with your brand kit. Export MP4s for YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and TikTok. A full-stack agentic video studio with 300+ Motion.md guides and support for 22 agents, including Claude Code, Codex, DSH, and WorkBuddy.

details.readme:
The open-source Claude Motion & CapCut alternative

Install · Agents · Use cases & remakes · Why OpenMotion · Setup & architecture · Community

**English** · [简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/README.ja.md)
# OpenMotion OpenMotion is a **full-stack agentic video** studio and an **open-source alternative to Claude Motion and CapCut**. Upload a reference video or paste a social video link to **recreate it with your own brand kit and copy**. - 🎬 **Full-stack video recreation.** Code video with HTML. Your agent breaks down the reference, rebuilds its shots and transitions, and generates missing assets. Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project. - 🔑 **BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys.** OpenMotion is free and open source. Recreate videos in [your local agent](#agent-wall) with your own API keys. Supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, and WorkBuddy. - 🧩 OpenMotion introduces **Motion.md**, a Markdown format for shot order, timing and transitions. Use it to share how a brand film works, shot by shot. - 🎛️ **Images, video, music and voice.** Create artwork with GPT Image 2.6, add a shot with Seedance 2.5, score it with Suno and narrate it with Eleven v4. [Explore the models and providers](#model-wall). ### Install from ChatGPT Marketplace **One-click installation. No manual configuration required.** Once installed, create motion videos from scratch, recreate reference videos, or start from a template—all in your conversation. **[Install OpenMotion in ChatGPT →](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6a742d13e88481919b42002864b1bb26)** ### Install in your agent Copy this instruction into your local agent to set up OpenMotion from source: ```text Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/install.md and follow the instructions to install and connect OpenMotion in the current agent. ``` After setup, the agent opens the local template library and shows the welcome followed by three project-preview cards in a self-contained HTML document. Each installation samples three distinct entries from the curated pool of five. The complete silent previews and posters are bundled, so this display does not wait for native MCP reload or fetch remote reference films. Native original-reference playback remains available separately and requires internet access. Automatic current-chat MCP activation is assessed independently. Preview a card, choose **Recreate template**, then send your brief to start creating. [Source installation guide](install.md) · [Onboarding selection](docs/install-onboarding.md#maintained-recommendation-selection) ### Install the published npm app (optional) Source setup above remains the default for repository installation. To explicitly choose the published application with prebuilt Studio and its configured online catalog, copy this instruction into your local agent: ```text Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/docs/install.md and follow the instructions to install and connect the published npm application in the current agent. ``` [Published application installation and channel selection](docs/install.md). Published versions can lag behind this checkout. ### Run the repository locally Use Git, npm and Node.js 26.11.1: ```sh git -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.required=false clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion.git cd openmotion npm ci npm run build:studio npm start ``` Open the actual `studioUrl` or `previewUrl` printed at startup, then choose **Template library**. Studio and MCP read the templates in this checkout. To connect your agent to this same copy, follow [source setup and MCP configuration](#agent-setup). [Clone size and optional media](docs/repository-storage.md) ### Start from an existing project Import a **HyperFrames project ZIP** into OpenMotion to continue editing its composition and local assets. Compress the project folder, open **All projects → Import projects**, then select the imported copy to edit in Studio or with your Agent. Import creates an independent copy and requires a supported native project structure. [Step-by-step import guide, required files and compatibility](docs/project-archives.md#import-from-hyperframes) **22 local agents** · [Choose your agent](#choose-agent)

## 🎞️ Use cases and remake examples Explore product demos, brand films, talking-head videos and more. The previews below show reference videos. **[Browse the full template library →](https://open-design.ai/templates/)** — Find more templates, full videos, Motion.md and recreation instructions. ### AI recuts & revisions

OpenAI · Build a story from multiple scenes
Connect different scenes around one narrative idea, then expand into a broader montage.
View template

Layer clips and screenshots in sequence, keeping the main title readable above them.
View template
### Product launches & demos

Notion · Show a problem, then the solution
Move from crowded tasks to coordinated agents; adapt the sequence to your own product.
View template

Build momentum with overlapping requests, then reveal the app in one clear beat.
View template

Kimi · Connect worlds through motion
Use code strips, offset slices and transitions to connect a series of brand scenes.
View template
Slack · Rebuild a brand mark
Break a mark into simple shapes and reassemble it with your own colors and name.
View template

details.readme:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 9. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, share, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | | `/reverse-any-video` | Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro. | | `/style-sampling` | Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? repository.description: A 3D UI system for Unreal Engine 5.8: world-space and screen-space widgets, widget Blueprints with a UMG-style designer, a native control library, .dui text authoring and tween animation. A fork of LGUI.

details.readme:
DreamGUI

A 3D UI system for Unreal Engine 5.8.

A widget is a UObject with a rect, anchors and a pivot, arranged in a tree and batched by a canvas into as few draw calls as it can — on the screen, or standing in the level at any angle with correct hit testing either way. A UI tree is a widget Blueprint you subclass, written as .dui text or in a UMG-style designer that edits the same class. A control library, tweens, per-player input and gamepad navigation come with it.

中文文档  ·  Documentation  ·  Getting started  ·  .dui language  ·  Class reference  ·  Changelog

> [!TIP] > Keep every `.dui` file in version control next to the widget Blueprint it is the source of. The Blueprint's > hierarchy is compiled from the file, and a property changed in the designer is written back into it, so the text > is what a review, a diff and a merge read. > [!NOTE] > **1.0.0 is the first public release.** The fork's development builds before it were numbered 1.x, 2.0.0 and > 2.1.0 (commits `2416e3f8`, `3049561a` on `main`); a project on one of them reads > [Docs/guides/migration.md](Docs/guides/migration.md#from-21-to-100) — 1.0.0 carries no CoreRedirects, so assets saved by those > builds, or against LGUI and LexUI, are resaved once before they are opened with it. DreamGUI is a fork of > [LGUI / LexUI](https://github.com/liufei2008/LGUI) by Lex Liu, MIT licensed — not a drop-in replacement for it. --- ## What it looks like ```text class /Game/UI/WBP_Settings use "UI/Library.dui" as ui VerticalBox Root : ui.Page { Spacing = 24 Text Title : ui.Heading { Text = "Settings" } rows ui.Row : ui.Wide (Label, Value) { "Subtitles", "On" "Difficulty", "Normal" "Vibration", "Off" } Native.Button Apply { Text { Text = "Apply" } OnClicked -> HandleApply } Text Hint : ui.Note { Shown <- bDirty Text = "Unsaved changes" } } ``` A library supplies the styles and the `Row` component, `rows` writes one instance per line, the button routes its click to a function on the user widget, and the hint shows while a variable says so. Compiled, the file is an ordinary widget Blueprint — a `UDreamWidgetBlueprint` whose class is a `UDreamUserWidget`: ```cpp UDreamUIBPLibrary::AddWidgetOfClassToViewport(this, WBP_Settings); // a layer on the screen ``` or dragged into a level, an `ADreamWorldWidgetActor` — the same class as a surface in the world. ## Quick start 1. Clone into the project's `Plugins/` directory, regenerate project files and build: ```bash git clone https://github.com/TypeDreamMoon/DreamGUI.git Plugins/DreamGUI ``` That is the whole install for a fresh project, on a launcher install too: the plugin compiles against the engine's public headers only and carries its own generated msdfgen copy under `ThirdParty/`. 2. Open [`Content/Samples/HelloDreamGUI.dui`](Content/Samples/HelloDreamGUI.dui) — the smallest file that is still a real screen. Make a widget Blueprint for it (*Content Browser ▸ Add ▸ DreamGUI Widget*) with **DreamUI Text User Widget** (`UDreamTextUserWidget`) as its parent class — only such a class shows *Set Source File…* in the designer toolbar — point it at the file, and compile. 3. Show it: in a graph, **Create Dream Widget** then **Add to Viewport**, as with UMG -- the file's `props` are pins on the create node; in C++, `UDreamUIBPLibrary::AddWidgetOfClassToViewport`. Or drag the Blueprint into a level. The screen root, the raycaster and the event system are created on demand; nothing else needs configuring. Two settings are worth making early — the game viewport client for non-US keyboard layouts, and the Slate input source for the engine's UI-only input mode. Both are on [Installation](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/start/installation). ## What's in it | | | | :-- | :-- | | **Widgets and canvases** | Rects with anchors and a pivot, visuals that draw (text, images, rect blocks, polygons, rings, lines), a canvas that walks only the widgets that changed and patches its sections in place | | **Screen and world** | Screen space, world space at any angle (DreamGUI's own renderer, or the engine's pipeline for post process and depth), render targets on any mesh; per-widget perspective; render transforms in three dimensions | | **Widget Blueprints** | A tree is a class: subclass it, nest it, fill its named slots, reach its children by name; the designer edits the class directly, rebuilt against UMG's | | **`.dui`** | Nodes, styles, resources, `use … as` libraries, components written in `.dui` with `props`, `events` and slots, bindings and routes, `if` / `for` / `each`, `rows` tables, timelines — every mistake a `DUInnnn` code with its line and column | | **Layout** | UMG-shaped panels on a layout engine rebuilt along Blink's and Yoga's lines: const measurement, immutable fragments, invalidation with a reason | | **Text** | Distance-field glyphs that stay sharp at any scale or angle, small text as crisp as Slate's, colour emoji, fallback faces, best fit, gradient text, culture-aware line breaking | | **Controls** | Buttons, toggles, sliders, spin boxes, text inputs, dropdowns, list, tile and tree views, dialogs, tab views, ring menus … named as UMG names them, with style structs and style sheets | | **Input** | Per-player pointers, focus and text targets; Tab and gamepad navigation; modals, popups, tooltips, drag and drop; an optional Slate input source | | **Animation** | Tweens, render-transform tweens for widgets inside panels, widget animations Sequencer edits, and `.dui` timelines | ## How it differs from UMG The difference is structural rather than cosmetic, so it is worth knowing before committing to either. | | UMG / Slate | DreamGUI | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | Widget | `SWidget`, retained-mode Slate | `UObject` in a component-like tree | | Sizing | Content-sized: a widget's size **is** its desired size | Box-first: you author a rect, content is arranged inside it | | Text | The box grows to the text | The text is aligned in the box, and may overflow it | | Placement | Slot-relative | Anchors + pivot, resolution-independent | | In-world | `WidgetComponent`, a rendered quad | A first-class render mode | The vocabulary deliberately does not differ: a control answers to the name its UMG counterpart uses, and `Resources/UMGParity` records, for 58 UMG classes and some 960 members, which names were adopted, mapped or rejected and why — held against UMG's own reflection by the automation suite. ## Documentation The canonical English manual starts at [Docs/README.md](Docs/README.md). The manual is published at **** in Chinese and English. | | | | :-- | :-- | | **[Getting started](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/start/installation)** | install, a first screen, the project layout and the authoring loop | | **[Concepts](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/concepts/widgets)** | widgets, canvases, world space, widget Blueprints, layout, text, rendering, input, animation | | **[The .dui language](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/dui/overview)** | every construct of the language, page by page — also in the repository as [Docs/language/index.md](Docs/language/index.md) | | **[Controls](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/controls)** | the control library, styles and style sheets, UMG parity | | **[Class reference](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/reference)** | every public class, printed from reflection — also as [Docs/Reference](Docs/Reference/index.md) | | **[Diagnostics](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/diagnostics)** | every `DUInnnn` code: what it means, how it happens, how to fix it | | **[Guides](https://gui.toolchain.64hz.cn/en/docs/guides/fonts-and-packaging)** | fonts and packaging, moving from LGUI / LexUI, upgrading, platforms — [Docs/guides/migration.md](Docs/guides/migration.md), [Docs/guides/fonts-and-packaging.md](Docs/guides/fonts-and-packaging.md) | | **[Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)** | what each version changed | ## Editor and tooling | | | | :-- | :-- | | **Designer** | Picking by rect, hover feedback, per-axis resize handles, a rotate handle (Shift for 15° steps), an anchor medallion, marquee selection, drag to reparent, Content Browser drops, palette favourites and search, undo; the *Events* section creates a handler and its route in one click. On a class a `.dui` is the source of, a property edit is written back onto its line in the file, and a structural edit is refused with the reason — the hierarchy is the file's | | **[VS Code extension](https://github.com/TypeDreamMoon/dreamgui-language-support)** | Highlighting, completion, hover, navigation, diagnostics and formatting for `.dui`, with the compiler's own codes | | **`DreamUI.Capture`** | a PNG of the viewport and of every render-target canvas (`UDreamUICaptureLibrary` from Blueprint) | | **`DreamUI.Stats`** | what the frames since the last call cost, stage by stage, with batches, vertices and bytes; every stage is a `DreamUI_*` scope in Unreal Insights | | **`DreamGUI.Memory`** | what the fonts, atlases and canvases hold | | **Automation suite** | `Automation RunTests DreamGUI`, or by preset with `Tools/Tests/Invoke-DreamGUITests.ps1`; static checks for module layering and engine-private includes | | **[`Tools/Bench`](Tools/Bench/README.md)** | the benchmarks the performance work was measured with: a screen of 5000 turning buttons and a level of 2688 world-space panels | ## Modules ```text L4 DreamGUISamples L3 DreamGUIControls DreamGUIExtensions L2 DreamGUIInput L1 DreamGUI (core) L0 DreamGUIRenderer DreamTween ------------------------------------------------------------ DreamGUIEditor, DreamGUIK2Nodes (uncooked only), DreamGUITests (editor only) ``` A module depends only on modules in the layers below its own, and a static check fails an include that goes the other way. C++ that uses a type from a module other than the core adds that mod

repository.description: An AI agent skill for organizing travel footage, planning scenes and revising films in your preferred editor. Not a standalone video editor.

details.readme:
# Family Travel Editor **A free AI skill for Claude Code and Codex that helps you turn travel footage into a film.** Organize your clips, recover the story behind them and work through edits with your agent. Use it with your video editor; it is not a standalone editing app. [**Start with one scene**](#start-with-one-scene) [Watch the overview](#watch-how-it-works) [What’s New in v0.4.0](docs/whats-new-v0.4.0.md) [Capabilities and limits](docs/capabilities.md) **Use Final Cut Pro on Mac:** assemble an editable timeline through FCPXML and an optional MCP connection, then continue in Final Cut. [Setup, tested operations and limits](skills/family-travel-editor/references/final-cut.md). **Use CapCut Web:** assemble and revise an editable cloud timeline through the optional official plugin. [Setup, tested operations and export limits](skills/family-travel-editor/references/capcut.md). ## Watch how it works [**▶ Watch on YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FP_AA2khgtM). 1:45. English ## Start with one scene 1. **[Download the v0.4.0 source ZIP](https://github.com/denyakortunov/family-travel-editor/releases/download/v0.4.0/family-travel-editor-source-v0.4.0.zip)** and unzip it. Open the extracted folder in your local AI agent. 2. Ask: **“Read `skills/family-travel-editor/SKILL.md` and help me get started. Ask about my trip and footage, build a short brief and guide me to the next step.”** 3. Answer in your own words. The agent asks about **your trip and footage, the kind of film you want, and any editor you already use**. “Suggest something” and “I haven’t chosen an editor” are valid answers. It saves the brief and proposes a first scene once it can inspect the material. Installation alone does not open a chat. Invoke `$family-travel-editor` or use the prompt above to start the guided brief; you do not need a finished scene idea. Python 3.9+ is needed for helper checks, not for answering the brief in chat. Inspecting picture and sound requires suitable tools; a file catalogue alone does not mean the footage has been watched. [Installation, first prompt, returning tomorrow and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started.md)
Install permanently in Codex or another compatible agent From the extracted repository root: ```sh python3 tools/install_skill.py --destination ~/.agents/skills ``` Open a new chat and invoke `$family-travel-editor`, or use the absolute SKILL.md path printed by the installer. If you already use `~/.codex/skills`, update that location to avoid duplicate copies. Alternatively, use the optional [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) and choose your agent when prompted: ```sh npx skills add https://github.com/denyakortunov/family-travel-editor/tree/v0.4.0/skills/family-travel-editor ``` The CLI needs Node.js; the Python installer does not. See the [update and backup guide](docs/getting-started.md#6-update-or-undo-an-update).
## How it works [Explore each step and a worked story example](docs/from-footage-to-film.md) Dropbox Replay is optional. Review in your editor or an AI preview when your connected tools support it, then give feedback with a version and timecode. Keep the scene plan, preferences and timecoded feedback in your film workspace. They give the next session a record of what was decided and what still needs work. The included helpers catalogue files, render **silent video previews** and prepare **video-only Resolve XML**. Full sound mixing, titles and direct editor control need separately available tools. The bundled Resolve import/playback/export route remains unvalidated. For other editors, use the [manual assembly plan](docs/manual-assembly.md) unless you have a tested integration. ## Try a concrete example - **[Grand Canyon picture edit](examples/grand-canyon-sunset/README.md):** three real source clips become 24 seconds, then a bounded revision makes it 22 seconds. Clips and both silent previews are included in the source ZIP. - **[From memory to a scene plan](examples/memory-to-plan/README.md):** an author's answer becomes a provisional plan and a revision. This is a planning example without inspected footage or a finished film. - **[Synthetic trimming exercise](examples/story-to-cut/README.md):** exact source ranges and a two-second trim for checking helper behavior. ## Why I made this I film our family trips on a DJI Osmo Pocket 3 and drones. Editing a film usually takes me 20–30 hours, so footage can sit untouched for years. I built this skill to give an agent a repeatable process and keep useful decisions between sessions. It still takes editorial work; time savings have not been measured. One useful question was why we went to the mountains. My answer: we wanted cooler weather than Singapore. That gives sweaters, tea and a fireplace a shared meaning. The next step is to find the actual shots that tell that story.
Tools and budget ### Tools and budget The skill and helper scripts are free and open source. Your agent, editor and optional services have their own costs. Use the tools you already have; a paid editor is not required to start planning. - Python runs the local helpers. FFmpeg and ffprobe are needed for the optional silent preview. - Use your preferred editor. [Editor choices and integration limits](skills/family-travel-editor/references/editors.md) explain the supported routes. - Photos, selected travel records and licensed music libraries are optional. Your own answers can supply travel context. - For sound work, see [Fairlight mix checks](skills/family-travel-editor/references/fairlight.md), [music and sound timing](skills/family-travel-editor/references/scene-music.md) and the [optional Epidemic Sound guide](skills/family-travel-editor/references/epidemic-sound.md).
## Data and help The bundled Python helpers run locally without network calls. Your agent and connected tools may send material to their providers according to your setup. Keep private footage, credentials and travel records out of public issues. [Tell us where you got stuck](https://github.com/denyakortunov/family-travel-editor/issues/new/choose), including the skill version, agent/editor and confusing step. [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) [Validation](docs/validation.md) [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) [Release history](docs/release-notes.md). Original code and instructions: [MIT](LICENSE). [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Independent project by [Denis Kortunov](https://github.com/denyakortunov).

details.readme:
# Estella **A 2D and 3D game engine whose editor is an MCP server.**
Your AI agent builds the game with the same 167 tools the editor's own UI uses — then ships it to the web, mini-game platforms, playable ads, desktop and native mobile. [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/esengine/estella)](https://github.com/esengine/estella/releases) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-167_tools-8A2BE2.svg)](https://estellaengine.com/docs/agents/mcp/) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Web%20%7C%20Mini--games%20%7C%20Playable%20ads%20%7C%20Desktop%20%7C%20Android%20%7C%20iOS-green.svg)](https://estellaengine.com/docs/publishing/overview/) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ask-DeepWiki-1f6feb.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/esengine/estella) [Website](https://estellaengine.com)  ·  [Agent](#your-agent-drives-the-editor)  ·  [Getting Started](#getting-started)  ·  [Documentation](#documentation)  ·  [QQ群 481923584](https://qm.qq.com/q/BONa5LXQ0U)
Every frame is one MCP tool call into the editor, captured as it happened — no mouse involved.
## Your agent drives the editor The Estella editor speaks the **Model Context Protocol**. Connect Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client, and the agent works inside the real editor rather than around it: - **It builds** — creates projects, spawns entities from the editor's own Create catalog, writes component fields, makes prefabs, paints tilemaps, writes and type-checks scripts. - **It looks** — takes screenshots of the viewport and the running game, replays a frame draw by draw, compares the game with reference images, and audits what a scene's look lacks. - **It plays** — enters Play mode, steps time deterministically, sends input and clicks UI by name, runs scripted playtests, then reads the running world back. - **It makes assets** — images, sound effects, music and 3D models, each answered with a picture of what it made. - **It ships** — reads project health, exports the game, and drives a build running on a connected phone. Every call goes through the editor's command surface: each one is **one undo step**, you watch it happen in the window, and you can take the mouse back at any time. The editor starts **read-only**; an agent edits only after you allow it in *Window → Connect AI Tools…*, which also writes the client's MCP config for you. | Group | What the agent gets | |---|---| | core | scene tree, entities, components, play / step / input, screenshots, logs, undo | | `assets` · `prefab` · `authoring` | asset documents and import settings, tilemaps, prefabs and variants, physics bodies, UI events | | `look` · `render` | reference images beside the game, light and field sweeps, frame capture and replay, shadows, LOD, bakes | | `code` · `project` | scripts, symbol search, type-check, project settings, health, export | | `image` · `sound` · `modeling` | draw sprites and textures, compose sound and music, build 3D models from steps | | `play` · `view` · `device` | gamepads, time scale, scripted playtests, editor view, and a game running on a connected phone | → [Connecting an agent](https://estellaengine.com/docs/agents/mcp/) ## Why Estella, when Unity and Unreal have MCP too? An MCP server can be bolted onto any editor. What an agent can actually get done depends on what sits behind it. - **The protocol is the editor, not a plugin on it.** The 167 tools call the pipelines the editor's own menus, inspector and toolbar run, so an agent's edit is the edit a person would have made, and undoes the same way. Calls are schema-checked and permission-gated by the editor itself. - **The agent can check its own work.** It steps a paused game frame by frame, so "play three seconds, then look" is the same frame every run. It sees the game, not just the log: screenshots, a frame replayed draw call by draw call, the game set beside a reference image, scripted playtests that read the running world back. - **The agent can make what the game needs.** Sprites, textures, sound effects, music and 3D models come from tools inside the editor, so a prototype does not stop at grey boxes while someone opens five other programs. - **Everything is text.** Scenes, prefabs and materials are JSON; gameplay is TypeScript. An agent reads and writes the project directly, and every change is a reviewable diff. - **It ships where heavier engines struggle.** A WebAssembly runtime that loads on a phone browser, seven Chinese mini-game platforms, single-file playable ads for the major ad networks, and native Android / iOS apps — from one project. - **It is open.** The runtime, SDK, pipeline and CLI are Apache-2.0: no royalties, no seats, no runtime fees. The editor is a free download. ## Rendered in real time

One day on the Amazon Lumberyard Bistro, recorded frame by frame from the running game: a sun that follows the clock, weather that turns from clear to mist, rain and snow, baked bounce light, reflections and volumetric haze. Scene © Amazon Lumberyard, CC BY 4.0, modified.

Space Frigate, a game made with Estella and recorded frame by frame as it runs: flying on thrusters, gunnery, and a jump through a gate to another star system. Every model, texture and sound in it is generated from a recipe.
## What's inside Estella is a C++ engine with a TypeScript SDK. The core runs as WebAssembly on the web and natively on desktop and mobile; game logic is written as ECS systems in TypeScript. **2D** — sprites and sprite animation, tilemaps (with LDtk import), Spine 2.1 – 4.3 and DragonBones, 2D lights and shadows, UI with layout, rich and bitmap text, particles, Box2D physics, native 2D rigs. **3D** — glTF / FBX import, PBR materials, directional / point / spot lights with shadows, sky atmosphere with time of day and weather, baked lightmaps, light and reflection probes, SSR, SSGI, height fog, terrain, water, foliage, skeletal animation with spring bones, navigation, Jolt or PhysX physics, streamed large worlds. **Everywhere** — one renderer for 2D and 3D on WebGL 2 and WebGPU, and one project exports to: | Target | What you get | |---|---| | Web | a static, self-contained build | | Mini-games | WeChat, Douyin, Kuaishou, Bilibili, Alipay, Huawei and quick games | | Playable ads | one inlined `index.html` for Meta, Google, Unity, AppLovin, Mintegral, TikTok / Pangle and MRAID networks | | Desktop | a native app on Windows, macOS and Linux — no Chromium | | Android / iOS | a native arm64 app on Vulkan / Metal — not a WebView | ## Getting Started **Install.** Download the editor for Windows or macOS from [estellaengine.com](https://estellaengine.com/#download) — always the newest release. Every build is also on the [releases page](https://github.com/esengine/estella/releases). **Create a project.** Open the editor, click **New Project**, pick a template. **Write a system.** ```typescript import { defineComponent, defineSystem, addSystem, Query, Mut, Res, Time, LocalTransform } from 'esengine'; const Speed = defineComponent('Speed', { value: 200 }); addSystem(defineSystem( [Res(Time), Query(Mut(LocalTransform), Speed)], (time, query) => { for (const [entity, transform, speed] of query) { transform.position.x += speed.value * time.delta; } } )); ``` Press **F5** to play — or connect your agent and ask it to do all three. ##

details.readme:
**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) > **中文文档入口：[文档目录](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [安装与启动](docs/getting-started.md) · [开发指南](docs/development.md)**
# SoduWork ## The AI-native engine for teams and their agents **A chat ends with an answer. A SoduWork request ends when the person who asked signs off.** **Multi-harness · Multi-agent · Self-hosted** Works with Pi · OpenCode · DeepSeek Harness · Qwen Code · Kimi Code · Codex Harness · Codex ```sh git clone https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork cd SoduWork ``` | Platform | Start command | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `sh start.sh --desktop` | | Windows PowerShell | `.\start.cmd --desktop` | | Windows Command Prompt | `start.cmd --desktop` | [Website](https://soduwork.ai) | [Live demo](https://soduwork.ai) | [Documentation](docs/README.md) | [Docs website](https://dev.soduwork.ai) | [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mdiri-ai/SoduWork)](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#quick-start) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2.svg)](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)
--- ## What SoduWork can do for you | | | | --- | --- | | **One harness does the work, another reviews it** | Pick Pi to do the work. OpenCode, on a different model, reviews it against the acceptance criteria. If the review fails, the work goes back with the reasons. | | **Hand a request to a colleague's agent** | People and AI work together: you file a request, AI writes the acceptance criteria, and you assign it to yourself or a colleague. The assignee's agent does the work and reviews it, and a person signs off. Everyone on the request can see who did what. | | **Turn one person's know-how into a team asset** | When you and AI get a task right, save the chat as a plugin. After review, anyone on the team can use it and contribute improvements, with access granted as needed. | ## Core ideas
**🔀 Smart dispatch** **The right agent and model for each job.** - Pick a harness for each step and switch mid-conversation - Routine steps on cheap or local models, strong models where it matters - Long tasks go to your own cloud runner **🛡️ Built-in governance** **Your organization decides which AI does what, and where.** - Plugins are reviewed before they are shared, granted to teams or people, and can be revoked - Roles, usage, cost and an audit log - Self-hosted **✅ Verified delivery** **Set the bar first. Done means the requester signed off.** - Every request carries its acceptance criteria - A separate AI review checks each one - A person makes the final call
## Quick start > SoduWork is in public beta. Try it and tell us what you think, and evaluate it before using it in production. You need Python 3.12+, Node.js 22.19+ and Git. From the cloned repository, run `sh start.sh --desktop` on macOS/Linux, `.\start.cmd --desktop` in Windows PowerShell, or `start.cmd --desktop` in Command Prompt. The first run installs dependencies, then starts the Hub, the admin console and the desktop client on this computer. Set a password for the `admin` account (12–128 characters) when asked. Then add a model provider under **Model catalog** in the admin console, start a chat in the client and try a small task. Pi is built in. ### Already added an API key? Start here 1. **Add a chat model as well.** Under **Capabilities → Model catalog**, find the service you connected, choose **Add model**, enter the provider's exact model ID, select **Chat model**, and save. Saving a service credential alone does not create a selectable model. 2. **Open the desktop client and sign in to the same Hub.** Use `--desktop` when starting from source. The browser admin console configures the service; check that **Connection** on the desktop sign-in screen points to that same Hub. 3. **Choose New conversation, Pi, and the model you added.** Pi uses the SoduWork model catalog. Codex uses its own account and needs its own sign-in; it does not automatically use this API key. 4. **Try a small task.** For example: “Turn these fictional meeting notes into an action table with owner and due date. Mark missing information as unconfirmed: Alex will organize the requirements by Friday; Sam will check the quotation.” Check the returned table against the notes. 5. **Create a requirement when you need assignment and acceptance.** Describe the goal, inputs and acceptance criteria, open **Arrange execution**, choose an Agent and model, and inspect the delivery before accepting it. A normal conversation does not require a project, plugin or automation first. For the first message, use an **OpenAI-compatible chat model with Pi**. A successful connection probe does not guarantee a successful inference: balance, model permissions and protocol support still matter. If the Agent list is empty, check **Agent management** and the Runner connection. If the model list is empty, check that the model exists, is enabled, and both interfaces use the same Hub. See [Run from source: send your first AI message](docs/getting-started.en.md#send-your-first-ai-message) for field-by-field setup and troubleshooting.
Try the live demo Download the client from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest), enter `https://service.soduwork.ai` under **Connection** on the sign-in screen, then sign up and sign in. > The demo is for evaluation only. Don't upload real business data or anything sensitive.
Install the desktop client Follow the illustrated [desktop installation and first conversation guide](docs/desktop-quickstart.en.md). | OS | Package | | --- | --- | | Windows | `SoduWork--Setup.exe` | | macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `SoduWork--mac-.dmg` | | Linux | `SoduWork--linux.deb` / `.rpm` / `.tar.gz` | Download from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases). On first launch, enter your Hub address under **Connection**, then sign in. On macOS, if you see "cannot verify the developer", open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**.
Deploy for a team with Docker With Docker installed and running, from the repository root: ```bash python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py up python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py credentials # show the initial admin password ``` This starts the Hub, the admin console and PostgreSQL on one server. Put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it to open it to your team. See [Deploy with Docker](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/docker) and [Deploy for a team](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/deploy).
Ports, data folders and troubleshooting are in [Run from source](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/run-from-source) and the [FAQ](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/faq). ## Why SoduWork AI agents give everyone fast output. What no one gets for free is trust in that output — or a way to keep what worked. That's where individuals and teams get stuck alike: | The problem | What SoduWork does | | --- | --- | | **Fast output, slow trust** — whether you work alone or in a team, the time AI saves goes back into checking what it produced | **The request is the spec.** Criteria set before work starts; a separate AI review checks each one; a person signs off | | **What worked dies in a chat thread** — for one person, it's last month's perfect run you can't reproduce; for a team, it's one person's method nobody else can use | **Get it right once, keep it as a plugin.** Reuse it yourself or publish it for everyone — every improvement reaches everyone | | **A drawer full of AI tools** — three subscriptions and no standard for which one does what | **One workbench, your playbook.** Your plugins run on every harness. Switch mid-conversation, keep your history and files | | **Results that never enter the workflow** — output gets copy-pasted around, and every handoff re-explains the background | **Issues that carry the context.** People and agents pick up where it left off, with a full record of who did what | ## How it works Requests, execution, review and reuse all happen in one shared issue pool: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raise a request] --> B[AI refines it
adds acceptance criteria] B --> C[Assign
yourself · a colleague · an agent] C --> D[Agent runs it
with a team plugin] D --> E[AI review
assignee confirms] E --> F[Requester signs off] F --> G[Save as a plugin] G -.reused by the team.-> D ``` | Role | Where they join | | --- | --- | | **Solo developer** | Puts requests in the pool, lets agents work through them, and only signs off | | **Specialist** | Gets a task right with AI, saves the method as a plugin, and publishes it to the team | | **Manager** | Drops in a request; AI fills in the criteria and routes it to a person or an agent; signs off at the end | | **New team member** | Uses the plugins the organization has built up to do the work to team standards, and improves them when they find a gap | Who asked, who did the work, which plugin ran and who approved it is always on record. ## Multi-harness · Multi-agent A harness is the agent runtime that does the work. It is not the model. SoduWork connects every harness through one adapter interface, so issues, plugins and review don't depend on any single harness. Switch harnesses mid-conversation and keep the history and the working folder. Programs that support the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) can be added with a catalog declaration.
Supported harnesses (9) | Harness | Models | How it connects | | --- | --- | --- | | Pi | Your SoduWork models | Built in | | OpenCode | Your SoduWork models | Native adapter, installed on demand | | DeepSeek Harness | Your SoduWork models, or your own DeepSeek key | ACP, installed on demand | | Qwen Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Kimi Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex Harness | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex | Its own OpenAI account | Native adapter, installed on demand |
Agents work together at several levels: | Level | Who decides | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | Harness | The harness itself | OpenCode or Qwen Code starts its own subagents to explore the code or split a task | | Single method | A Skill or plugin sets the method, process, rules and what counts as done | A review plugin tells the agent which checks to run and what evidence to attach | | Combined methods | A plugin workflow picks the harness, Skill and model for each step | Pi drafts, Qwen Code checks the sources, and the run stops if the check fails | | People and agents | The requester and the assignee or their agent | A request goes to a colleague, their agent does the work, the requester signs off | | In parallel | The Hub | Different issues run on different agents at the same time, including on cloud runners | Between steps and between people, work moves the way the plugin and the assignee say. Agents don't hand work to other agents on their own. ## Plugins and apps A skill tells AI how to do something. An agent wraps AI into an assistant. SoduWork plugins and apps turn the way your team works into something that **runs, gets verified, improves and stays governed**. | | Skill | Agent | SoduWork plugin | SoduWork app | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **What it is** | A met

details.readme:
Awesome Jev Live

The evidence-graded Jev index that rebuilds itself every two hours.

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Deutsch · Português (Brasil) · Русский · Italiano · العربية · हिन्दी · Türkçe · Tiếng Việt · ไทย · Bahasa Indonesia · Polski · Nederlands · Українська

> [!NOTE] > **Live index** · Last sync: `2026-11-17T16:00:54+08:00` (UTC+8) > · Entries: **829** · Added in the latest update: **4** · Implementation languages: **26** Every entry below was collected, filtered and re-checked by the pipeline in this repository. Numbers and timestamps come from the sources, not from a hand-written snapshot. ## 🔥 Picks of the moment — the top of each category One entry per category, ranked by evidence grade and stars, recomputed on every update. A ranking, not an endorsement; every pick links through to its full card below. Projects that published a screenshot or a recording are preferred, so the strip stays visual.
🏛️ typesafe-ai/skills ⭐2905 · ✅ official Agent skills for building with TypeSafe's System One API 🧰 john-rocky/coreai-kit ⭐126 · Swift · 👁️ observed Swift SDK for running chat, vision and speech models on iPhone and Mac with Apple's Core AI. Model download and caching, FoundationModels integration, and runnable…
🤖 gargpratyush/jev-router ⭐670 · JavaScript · 🔎 inferred Route to the cheapest model in claude code for your task using jev-router 🛡️ dharmeshgurnani/codeotter ⭐3 · TypeScript · 👁️ observed Autonomous, self-hosted AI code reviews, calibrated scoring gauges, and merge gates from any open model.
🧪 Mapika/decider ⭐1055 · Python · 👁️ observed A family of System One-style models fine-tuned from Qwen3.5, designed for one-pass typed decisions with calibrated probabilities. 🔬 r-ms/mini-jev ⭐64 · Python · 🔎 inferred mini-Jev: what a Jev-style typed-decision interface looks like on a frozen Qwen3-4B — read the option letter's logits instead of generating JSON. Preregistered…
🎮 MCG-NJU/VideoJev ⭐311 · Python · 👁️ observed VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction 📰 9 known defects (jaggedness) ⭐0 · ✅ official 字面理解、**计数不可靠**、日期比较、多级间接、无关细节大 state、对抗内容、指令与 criteria 矛盾、结构性不变量、生成。官方建议"拆成原子问题在代码里组合"。
## Contents - [What is Jev](#what-is-jev) - [How entries are graded](#how-entries-are-graded) - [Official SDKs and developer tools](#official-sdks-and-developer-tools) — **6** - [Community clients, SDKs and adapters](#community-clients-sdks-and-adapters) — **143** - [Agent tooling: MCP, hooks, gates and coding agents](#agent-tooling-mcp-hooks-gates-and-coding-agents) — **251** - [Routing, guardrails and approvals](#routing-guardrails-and-approvals) — **64** - [Evaluation, calibration and benchmarks](#evaluation-calibration-and-benchmarks) — **90** - [Open reproductions, weights and architecture research](#open-reproductions-weights-and-architecture-research) — **68** - [Applications, games, robotics and interactive demos](#applications-games-robotics-and-interactive-demos) — **44** - [Writing, discussions and sibling lists](#writing-discussions-and-sibling-lists) — **75** - [Other projects](#other-projects) — **88** - [Projects by implementation language](#projects-by-implementation-language) ## What is Jev Jev is TypeSafe AI's first **System One model**. It does not write prose. It takes a state plus questions whose answer space you define in advance, and returns typed values with probability distributions your code can branch on. | | | | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Shape** | `state + typed questions` → `constrained answers + probabilities` → `your code` | | **Primitives** | `Choice` (pick one of ≤255 options), `Score` (a rubric 2–10), `Noul` (a probabilistic yes/no) | | **Endpoint** | `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, model `jev-1.13.0` / alias `jev-latest` | | **Good fits** | routing, triage, scoring, moderation, verification and low-latency gates inside a bounded workflow | | **Known limits** | counting is unreliable, multi-level indirection is weak, and official material names nine classes of jaggedness. Schema-valid output is not the same as a correct decision — calibrate on your own data. | ## How entries are graded Most lists in this space assert inclusion. This one says how much it actually verified, then lets you filter accordingly. | Grade | What it means | | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `official` | Published by TypeSafe AI itself. | | `observed` | A public artifact that can be opened and read — real source, real configuration, or an explicit TypeSafe/Jev declaration in the repository name or topic. | | `inferred` | Matched on an ambiguous signal plus corroborating vocabulary, but not yet read line by line. | | `unverified` | Looks related, nothing independently confirmed. repository.description: Enterprise Agent Harness & MCP Gateway: connect APIs, databases, file servers and 600+ connectors (SAP, Odoo, Etsy…) to Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and your agents. Memory, skills, knowledge graph, SSO/RBAC, audit log and governance built in. Your AI company brain.

details.readme:
AnythingMCP: the open-source MCP gateway that becomes your company brain

English · Deutsch · 简体中文 · 日本語

AnythingMCP is an open-source, self-hosted MCP gateway that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini to the software your company runs and to the documents on your file servers, without writing an MCP server.
On top of the gateway it keeps your company brain: a knowledge graph of how your systems connect, AI skills and company memory, shared by every AI client and limited by each user's role.
877 ready connectors with 12,000+ tools, among them SAP, Odoo, weclapp and Amazon Seller; 46 need no API key.

16,000+ workspaces on AnythingMCP Cloud · 1.5M+ AI tool calls a month · listed in the official Claude directory and the ChatGPT Plugin Directory

Try the Cloud free for 7 days · Add to Claude · Add to ChatGPT · Run it yourself · Docs · Connector guides · Discussions

**One question in Claude, answered from Etsy, SAP and a logistics API.** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc8c9ef3-11cf-4eab-aa4d-98472dc554b3 --- ## What your AI gets A gateway forwards calls. A company brain also knows where your documents are, how your systems connect and what your company has already decided. AnythingMCP gives every AI client both, through one MCP endpoint: | | What it does | Edition | |---|---|---| | **Every system, one endpoint** | 696 catalog connectors, or your own REST/OpenAPI, SOAP, GraphQL, OData, SQL, IMAP/SMTP or MCP source. Tools register at runtime. [Connectors](#connect-any-api-soap-service-or-database) | All | | **File Search** | Indexes SFTP, FTP/FTPS, WebDAV (Nextcloud, NAS), S3 or a network share: every PDF page, Excel rows with their column names, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook mails with attachments. The AI answers with file, page and date. [File Search](docs/connectors/file-search.md) | Cloud; self-hosted Enterprise | | **File Share** | Temporary download links for files from your folders, or for files the AI writes (a CSV export, a report), internal or public, with expiry and revoke. [File Share](docs/connectors/file-search.md) | Cloud; self-hosted Enterprise | | **Company memory** | Facts and preferences saved from one AI client and found again in any other: said once in Claude, used by Copilot. Personal and company scopes, with folders and role limits. [Memory](docs/memory.md) | Enterprise | | **AI skills** | The procedures your agents follow, written by hand or learned from real requests and fixed errors, approved by an admin. [AI skills](docs/knowledge-graph.md#ai-skills) | All | | **Learning projects** | Keep what an experienced colleague teaches the AI before they leave: their corrections on one MCP server become skills for the whole team, after they agree and confirm. [Learning projects](docs/learning-projects.md) | Team, Enterprise | | **Knowledge graph** | How your systems connect, so the agent links a customer in one system to their orders in another without being told. [Knowledge Graph](docs/knowledge-graph.md) | All | | **Code Mode** | One short program that calls several tools in an isolated sandbox with no secrets and no network, so a five-step lookup becomes one call. [Code Mode](docs/code-mode.md) | All; write access Enterprise | | **Governance** | Roles and per-tool permissions, response mapping that drops fields before they reach the model, an audit log of every call. SSO and SCIM from your directory. [Security](#security-and-governance) | All; SSO/SCIM Enterprise | The self-hosted Community edition is free under AGPL-3.0 for any use, including commercial use, for up to 3 active users, with unlimited connectors and MCP servers. More users, single sign-on, SCIM, File Search beyond the 30-day trial and support come with Enterprise, on request: [contact us](https://anythingmcp.com/contact?plan=enterprise). Administrators can try single sign-on and SCIM for 30 days under **Settings → License**. Existing Starter and Team licence keys keep working. --- ## Run it yourself Requires Docker 24+ and `openssl`; on macOS, start Docker Desktop first. No clone needed: ```bash mkdir anythingmcp && cd anythingmcp curl -fsSLo docker-compose.yml \ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HelpCode-ai/anythingmcp/main/docker-compose.quickstart.yml printf 'JWT_SECRET=%s\nENCRYPTION_KEY=%s\n' "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env docker compose up -d ``` Open and register: **the first account becomes admin**. Your MCP endpoint is `http://localhost:4000/mcp`, the API docs are at `http://localhost:4000/api/docs`. > **Keep the generated `.env`.** `ENCRYPTION_KEY` decrypts the credentials you store. Lose it and every connector has to be re-credentialed. On amd64 the image pulls in about 30 s and the API is healthy 24 s later. The image is amd64 only for now; the compose file pins the platform, so it also runs on Apple Silicon under emulation. The quickstart binds to `127.0.0.1` on purpose, because nothing in front of it terminates TLS. **For an instance other people or a cloud AI client can reach**, clone the repo and run `./setup.sh`: it asks for a domain, gets certificates through Caddy, generates the secrets and sets the MCP auth mode. See the [Deployment Guide](docs/deployment.md).
Other ways to run it: managed cloud, Railway, DigitalOcean
[**AnythingMCP Cloud**](https://cloud.anythingmcp.com) is the same AGPL code, operated by us in **Frankfurt, Germany**, with a 7-day free trial. Start there to try it on your own APIs, and move it in-house when you want the credentials to stop travelling; the connectors are the same either way. DPA/AVV on request via [info@helpcode.ai](mailto:info@helpcode.ai). SSO and SCIM are self-hosted only, with an Enterprise licence. [![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/deploy/8-X4WD?referralCode=k30bPV&utm_medium=integration&utm_source=template&utm_campaign=generic)   [![Install on DigitalOcean](https://www.deploytodo.com/do-btn-blue.svg)](https://marketplace.digitalocean.com/apps/anythingmcp)
--- ## How it works 1. **Add a connector.** Install an **adapter** from the catalog (a ready JSON definition for SAP, Odoo, DHL and the rest), or point AnythingMCP at your own OpenAPI spec, WSDL, GraphQL endpoint, Postman collection or database. Once configured in your workspace it is a **connector**, and each of its operations is an MCP tool. 2. **Decide what the model sees.** Rename and describe the tools in the visual editor, drop the fields that must not leave your network, and choose which roles may call which tools. 3. **Hand one URL to your AI client.** An **MCP server** is the endpoint you add to Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or Cursor. It exposes the connectors you assign to it, and nothing else. --- ## Connect any API, SOAP service or database Most companies have no MCP servers yet. They have a REST API, an ERP, a SOAP service from 2009 and a database. Each of them becomes a set of MCP tools: | Source | What you get | Docs | |---|---|---| | **OpenAPI / Swagger (REST)** | Import a spec by URL or paste it; every operation becomes a tool with parameters, auth and endpoint mapping filled in | [REST](docs/connectors/rest.md) · [guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/rest-api-to-mcp) · [demo: openapi-to-mcp](https://github.com/HelpCode-ai/openapi-to-mcp) | | **Postman collection, cURL** | Folders, auth, body modes and `{{variables}}` carry over; every request becomes a tool | [Postman import](docs/connectors/rest.md#from-postman-collection) | | **SOAP / WSDL** | Each operation becomes a tool; envelopes, parameter order and WCF services are handled for you | [SOAP](docs/connectors/soap.md) · [guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/soap-to-mcp) · [demo: soap-to-mcp](https://github.com/HelpCode-ai/soap-to-mcp) | | **GraphQL** | Introspection turns queries and mutations into tools, or you define the operations yourself | [GraphQL](docs/connectors/graphql.md) · [guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/graphql-to-mcp) | | **OData** (SAP Gateway included) | Reads each service's `$metadata`, so the model sees entity sets, keys and SAP's business labels; V2 and V4 | [OData](docs/connectors/odata.md) · [guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/odata-to-mcp) | | **SQL and MongoDB** | PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, SAP HANA, SQLite and MongoDB: schema, example and query tools, read-only by default | [Database](docs/connectors/database.md) · [SAP HANA](docs/connectors/sap-hana.md) · [guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/database-to-mcp) · [demo: sql-to-mcp](https://github.com/HelpCode-ai/sql-to-mcp) | | **Email (IMAP/SMTP)** | Any mailbox (IONOS, Strato, GMX, T-Online, Gmail with an app password, your own mail server): list folders, search, read with attachments, flag, move, save drafts and send | [Email](docs/connectors/email.md) | | **Another MCP server** | Discover its tools and serve them next to your own, behind the same auth and audit | [MCP bridge](docs/connectors/mcp-bridge.md) | Tools register at runtime, without a restart.
